title: China-to-Latvia Wireless / IoT Device Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Cybersecurity — RED Art. 3.3(d)(e)(f) + EN 18031 + CERT.LV (Mandatory from 1 Aug 2025, Latvia / SPRK)
rows.target_requirement: Latvia applies EU cybersecurity requirements for radio equipment without national derogation. Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 activated RED Article 3.3(d), (e), and (f) for internet-connected radio equipment, equipment processing personal/location/traffic data, and equipment for children or wearables. Mandatory application date: 1 August 2025 (extended from 1 August 2024 by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2444). The harmonised standards are EN 18031-1:2024 (network security), EN 18031-2:2024 (privacy for personal data-processing devices), and EN 18031-3:2024 (child protection/fraud prevention), published in the EU Official Journal on 20 February 2025. SPRK enforces these requirements in Latvia as the national RED market surveillance authority. CERT.LV (Information Technology Security Incident Response Institution of the Republic of Latvia) operates as the national cybersecurity authority and coordinates with SPRK on cybersecurity incident response and product security matters. Products placed on the Latvian market from 1 August 2025 that fall within the scope of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 must include cybersecurity compliance in their DoC and technical file. The EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), expected to apply from 2027, will impose additional software security obligations for connected devices placed on any EU market including Latvia.
target_standards: Directive 2014/53/EU (RED), Art. 3.3(d)(e)(f)
Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 — activating RED Art. 3.3(d)(e)(f)
Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2444 — extending mandatory date to 1 August 2025
EN 18031-1:2024 — Radio equipment; common security requirements; Part 1: Internet connected radio equipment
EN 18031-2:2024 — Radio equipment; common security requirements; Part 2: Radio equipment processing personal data
EN 18031-3:2024 — Radio equipment; common security requirements; Part 3: Radio equipment for child protection and toys
Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act) — expected mandatory application from 2027 for connected products on EU market
CERT.LV — Information Technology Security Incident Response Institution of the Republic of Latvia; national cybersecurity authority coordinating with SPRK
rows.china_equivalent: China has IoT and network security requirements under MIIT Order No. 12 (2022) on IoT security administration, and voluntary national standards GB/T 36951-2018 (IoT sensor node security) and GB/T 37093-2018 (IoT data security). MIIT also enforces network access licence (NAL) requirements that include basic security criteria for telecom terminal equipment. However, none of these Chinese frameworks require pre-market security controls equivalent to EN 18031-1 (unique per-device credentials, no universal default passwords, software update integrity, attack surface minimisation). China has no regulatory analogue to RED Art. 3.3(d)-(f) as a mandatory CE-comparable pre-market cybersecurity gate.
china_standards: MIIT Order No. 12 (2022) — Administration of Internet of Things Security (MIIT)
GB/T 36951-2018 — Information security technology; IoT sensor network node security technical requirements (voluntary, SAMR/SAC)
GB/T 37093-2018 — Information security technology; IoT data security technical requirements (voluntary, SAMR/SAC)
rows.gap: This is the largest new compliance gap for Chinese Wi-Fi/IoT devices entering Latvia effective 1 August 2025. Specific EN 18031-1 mandatory controls that are absent from typical Chinese IoT product design include: (1) no universal default passwords — each device must ship with a unique credential or force the user to set one; (2) network interface disable capability — the device must support disabling all network access interfaces; (3) software update integrity — updates must be cryptographically signed and verified before installation; (4) encrypted communications — data in transit must be protected; (5) attack surface minimisation — all unused ports, protocols, and services disabled by default. Additionally: EN 18031-2 applies where the device processes personal data (most consumer IoT devices); EN 18031-3 applies to toys and childcare articles. SPRK may request cybersecurity technical documentation during market surveillance, and CERT.LV may flag imported products with known vulnerabilities for enforcement referral to SPRK. As a Baltic Sea EU member state with Riga Port serving as a regional electronics distribution hub, Latvian customs may screen devices for cybersecurity documentation gaps when entering the Baltic corridor. Looking ahead, the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) is expected to impose further mandatory software update, vulnerability disclosure, and SBOM obligations for connected products from approximately 2027, applying to Latvia as an EU member state.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory from 1 August 2025 for in-scope radio equipment under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 (as amended by (EU) 2023/2444); SPRK enforces in Latvia; CERT.LV coordinates cybersecurity matters; EU CRA (from ~2027) will add further obligations
mandatory_status.cn: No direct equivalent mandatory pre-market cybersecurity requirement; Chinese IoT security standards are voluntary or sector-specific; MIIT NAL includes basic security criteria only for telecom terminals

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] RED Art. 3.3(d)-(f) cybersecurity requirements, mandatory from 1 August 2025, represent the largest new gap for Chinese Wi-Fi/IoT devices entering Latvia. EN 18031-1/2/3 are the harmonised standards; no Chinese regulatory equivalent exists. SPRK enforces these requirements as the Latvian national market surveillance authority; CERT.LV coordinates on cybersecurity incident and product vulnerability matters. Manufacturers must conduct firmware/hardware security gap assessments and implement required controls before Latvian market placement from 1 August 2025. The forthcoming EU Cyber Resilience Act will impose additional obligations from approximately 2027.

rows.requirement: Electrical Safety — RED Art. 3.1(a) + EN IEC 62368-1 (Latvia 230 V/50 Hz, Plug C/F)
rows.target_requirement: Latvia applies EU harmonised electrical safety standards without national derogation. Under RED 2014/53/EU Art. 3.1(a), radio equipment must protect the health and safety of persons, domestic animals, and property. For Wi-Fi routers, IoT gateways, smart home devices, and Bluetooth accessories, the mandatory harmonised safety standard is EN IEC 62368-1:2020+A11:2021 (Audio/video, information and communication technology equipment — Part 1: Safety requirements). EN 60950-1 ceased to provide presumption of conformity on 20 December 2020 and is no longer acceptable. Latvia uses 230 V/50 Hz mains supply and plug types C (Europlug) and F (Schuko); mains-powered devices must be verified for compatibility with these supply parameters. Products must be labelled with the supply voltage/frequency in Latvian (in addition to other EU languages or symbols). SPRK enforces RED Art. 3.1(a); PTAC (Consumer Rights Protection Centre — Patērētāju tiesību aizsardzības centrs) enforces general product safety alongside.
target_standards: Directive 2014/53/EU (RED), Art. 3.1(a) — as transposed in Latvia
EN IEC 62368-1:2020+A11:2021 — Audio/video, information and communication technology equipment; Part 1: Safety requirements (harmonised under RED and LVD)
Directive 2014/35/EU (LVD) — Low Voltage Directive; may apply to standalone mains-powered accessories
rows.china_equivalent: In China, information technology equipment safety is governed by GB 4943.1-2022 (equivalent to IEC 62368-1:2018, second edition), mandatory under CCC (CNCA-C17-01) for IT equipment. Chinese mains supply is 220 V/50 Hz with plug types A and I (GB 2099 series); Chinese products are often designed for 100–240 V input, but the plug type will differ from Latvian C/F sockets. GB 4943.1-2022 aligns with IEC 62368-1 second edition, while EN IEC 62368-1:2020+A11:2021 is derived from the third edition with an EU-specific A11 amendment. Chinese CCC safety certificates do not satisfy RED Art. 3.1(a) conformity assessment in Latvia.
china_standards: GB 4943.1-2022 — Information technology equipment; safety; Part 1: General requirements (equivalent to IEC 62368-1:2018 2nd edition) (SAMR/CNCA, mandatory under CCC)
GB 2099 series — Plugs and socket-outlets for household and similar use (Chinese plug types A/I)
rows.gap: Four gaps apply for Chinese manufacturers exporting to Latvia: (1) Edition gap — EN IEC 62368-1:2020+A11:2021 (3rd edition + EU amendment) vs. GB 4943.1-2022 (2nd edition); A11 introduces additional fire enclosure and earthing conductor requirements absent from the Chinese standard; (2) Supply voltage/plug compatibility — China 220 V/A/I plug vs. Latvia 230 V/50 Hz/C/F; products must be tested and labelled for European supply parameters; (3) Chinese CCC test reports are insufficient for RED Art. 3.1(a) — re-testing at an EU-recognised laboratory is required; (4) EN 60950-1 is no longer valid and must not be cited in the DoC. PTAC may additionally enforce General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) obligations for consumer-facing devices.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — RED 2014/53/EU Art. 3.1(a); EN IEC 62368-1:2020+A11:2021 is the harmonised standard; 230 V/50 Hz / C/F plug required for Latvian mains-powered devices; SPRK and PTAC enforce
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for CCC-listed IT equipment — GB 4943.1-2022 under CNCA-C17-01 (SAMR); 220 V/50 Hz / A/I plug (domestic market)

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] EN IEC 62368-1:2020+A11:2021 is mandatory for electrical safety under RED Art. 3.1(a) in Latvia. EN 60950-1 is no longer valid. Chinese CCC tests to GB 4943.1-2022 (2nd edition) do not cover EU A11 requirements. Products must also be verified for 230 V/50 Hz operation and C/F plug compatibility. Re-testing at an EU-recognised laboratory and Latvian-language labelling of supply parameters are required.

rows.requirement: EMC — RED Art. 3.1(b) + EN 301 489 Series (Latvia / SPRK)
rows.target_requirement: Latvia applies EU harmonised EMC requirements without national derogation. Radio equipment must protect the radio spectrum and ensure adequate immunity under RED 2014/53/EU Art. 3.1(b). For Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices, the applicable harmonised standards are EN 301 489-1 v2.2.3 (common technical requirements) and EN 301 489-17 v3.2.4 (specific conditions for RLAN / Bluetooth broadband data transmission systems). These standards reference CISPR 32 emission limits and IEC 61000-4 immunity levels. SPRK is the national authority enforcing RED EMC requirements in Latvia; it can request test reports and DoC documentation from importers or EU Authorised Representatives at any time.
target_standards: Directive 2014/53/EU (RED), Art. 3.1(b) — as transposed in Latvia
EN 301 489-1 v2.2.3 — Electromagnetic compatibility and radio spectrum matters; common technical requirements
EN 301 489-17 v3.2.4 — Specific conditions for broadband data transmission systems (RLAN / Bluetooth)
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese EMC requirements for wireless devices are covered by GB/T 9254.1-2021 (emissions, equivalent to CISPR 32:2015) and GB/T 17618-2015 (immunity, equivalent to CISPR 24:2010), administered by SAMR/SAC. CCC-listed products are tested at CNCA-designated laboratories. While the underlying emission limits are broadly aligned with CISPR 32, EN 301 489-17 applies RLAN-specific test modes and duty-cycle-adjusted averaging not present in the Chinese GB/T framework. Chinese test reports are not accepted by SPRK as evidence of RED EMC conformity.
china_standards: GB/T 9254.1-2021 — Information technology equipment; radio disturbance characteristics (emissions, equivalent to CISPR 32:2015) (SAMR/SAC)
GB/T 17618-2015 — Information technology equipment; immunity characteristics (equivalent to CISPR 24:2010) (SAMR/SAC)
rows.gap: Chinese EMC test reports to GB/T 9254.1 / GB/T 17618 cannot substitute for EN 301 489-1 + EN 301 489-17 compliance in Latvia. Key gaps: (1) EN 301 489-17 applies RLAN-specific duty-cycle-adjusted emission averaging and dedicated test modes not present in GB/T 9254.1; (2) EU immunity test configurations under EN 301 489-1 reference specific IEC 61000-4 severity levels that may differ from Chinese test setups; (3) SPRK may request test reports citing the specific harmonised EN version — Chinese GB reports do not meet this evidential standard. Re-testing at an ILAC MRA-member or EU-accredited laboratory to EN 301 489-1 + EN 301 489-17 is required. Test reports must be retained for 10 years and made available to SPRK on request.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — RED 2014/53/EU Art. 3.1(b); covered under CE marking; SPRK enforces in Latvia
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for CCC-listed products; GB/T 9254.1 / GB/T 17618 under SAMR/SAC framework

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] RED Art. 3.1(b) EMC compliance for Wi-Fi/Bluetooth devices in Latvia requires EN 301 489-1 + EN 301 489-17 testing. Chinese GB/T 9254.1 / GB/T 17618 reports are not accepted. SPRK may request test documentation at any time. EU-accredited laboratory re-testing is required, and reports must be referenced in the DoC and retained for 10 years.

rows.requirement: EMC Directive 2014/30/EU — Applicability to Non-Radio EEE in Latvia
rows.target_requirement: For electrical or electronic products that are not radio equipment (i.e., do not contain a radio transmitter or receiver), Latvia applies the EMC Directive 2014/30/EU (transposed as EMCD) rather than RED. However, for the wireless/IoT device category covered by this dataset, RED 2014/53/EU is the primary applicable directive and its Art. 3.1(b) EMC essential requirement subsumes EMCD for in-scope radio equipment. Products that combine radio and non-radio functions (e.g., a smart home hub with both Wi-Fi and a wired Ethernet port) are assessed under RED for the radio elements; the non-radio elements may also need EMCD compliance if sold separately as standalone non-radio EEE. SPRK enforces EMCD for non-radio EEE alongside RED enforcement for radio equipment.
target_standards: Directive 2014/30/EU (EMCD) — Electromagnetic Compatibility Directive; applies to EEE not covered by RED
Directive 2014/53/EU (RED), Art. 3.1(b) — subsumes EMCD for radio equipment in scope
EN 55032:2015+A11:2020 — Electromagnetic compatibility of multimedia equipment; emission requirements (harmonised under EMCD)
rows.china_equivalent: China does not distinguish between radio and non-radio EMC frameworks in the same manner as the EU. GB/T 9254.1-2021 covers emissions for information technology equipment generally. The CCC mandatory certification scope under CNCA-C17-01 covers both radio-enabled and wired IT equipment under the same EMC standard framework. There is no Chinese regulatory analogue to the EU distinction between RED Art. 3.1(b) and the standalone EMCD for IT/AV equipment.
china_standards: GB/T 9254.1-2021 — Information technology equipment; radio disturbance characteristics (SAMR/SAC)
CCC CNCA-C17-01 — China Compulsory Certification for information technology equipment (SAMR/CNCA)
rows.gap: For wireless/IoT products exported from China to Latvia, RED Art. 3.1(b) is the primary EMC gate and the relevant EN 301 489 series standards must be applied. If the product also contains non-radio EEE functionality sold standalone or the product is borderline for RED scope, EMCD EN 55032 compliance may additionally be needed. Manufacturers should confirm product scope under RED Article 1 before selecting the conformity assessment route. SPRK enforces both RED and EMCD; incorrect directive selection is a common compliance deficiency found in market surveillance.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — EMCD 2014/30/EU for non-radio EEE; RED Art. 3.1(b) for radio equipment (primary pathway for wireless/IoT devices); both enforced by SPRK in Latvia
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB/T 9254.1 under CCC (CNCA-C17-01) for IT equipment EMC; no RED/EMCD distinction

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For wireless/IoT devices exported to Latvia, RED Art. 3.1(b) and EN 301 489 series are the mandatory EMC pathway; EMCD 2014/30/EU applies to any non-radio EEE component sold separately. Incorrect directive selection is a recognised market-surveillance risk in Latvia. Chinese GB/T EMC reports satisfy neither pathway. Manufacturers must confirm scope under RED Art. 1 and apply the correct harmonised standards.

source.publisher: EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the European Union

rows.requirement: EU Authorised Representative / Importer — Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 + Latvian Labelling
rows.target_requirement: Under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (Market Surveillance Regulation), Article 4, non-EU manufacturers must have either: (a) an importer established in the EU who takes on responsibility for the product, or (b) an EU Authorised Representative (EU AR) appointed by the manufacturer before the first product enters any EU market, including Latvia. The EU AR must be established in an EU member state (Latvia qualifies, but any EU member state suffices). The EU AR's name and postal address must appear on the product itself, its packaging, or its accompanying documentation in a visible and legible way. The same requirement applies when the product is sold through online platforms into Latvia. An EU AR is responsible for holding the DoC and technical documentation, cooperating with SPRK, and ensuring corrective action if the product is non-compliant. Latvian-language product labelling is a national requirement for products placed on the Latvian market: the product name, model identifier, manufacturer name and address, EU AR name and address, and any safety warnings must be provided in Latvian (Latin script). PTAC enforces labelling and general product safety requirements; SPRK enforces the EU AR documentation obligation under RED.
target_standards: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, Art. 4 — EU Authorised Representative obligation for non-EU manufacturers
Directive 2014/53/EU (RED), Art. 10 — manufacturer obligations including DoC and technical file retention
Directive 2014/53/EU (RED), Art. 11 — importer obligations
Latvian Consumer Rights Protection Law (Patērētāju tiesību aizsardzības likums) — consumer protection, including Latvian-language labelling obligation
EU General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) (EU) 2023/988 — applies from 13 December 2024 for consumer products
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent to the EU Authorised Representative obligation. Chinese manufacturers exporting to Latvia do not need to appoint any representative within China for EU regulatory purposes; however, they must appoint an EU-established entity (EU AR or importer) before the product enters any EU member state market. China's domestic market requires the manufacturer's Chinese address to appear on product packaging, but there is no obligation for a third-country representative structure analogous to the EU AR. Chinese CCC certificates list the manufacturer's Chinese address; this does not satisfy the EU requirement for an EU-based contact point.
china_standards: CCC — China Compulsory Certification; lists manufacturer's Chinese address but has no EU AR equivalent
GB 191-2008 / SJ/T 11364-2014 — Chinese product labelling standards (Chinese language only)
rows.gap: Structural gaps with no Chinese equivalent: (1) EU Authorised Representative — Chinese manufacturers without an EU importer must appoint an EU-established AR before first placement in Latvia or any EU market; failure renders the product non-compliant and prevents lawful customs clearance; (2) Latvian-language labelling — product labelling (name, model, manufacturer/EU AR contact, safety warnings, supply voltage) must include Latvian in Latin script; English-only or Chinese-only labels are not acceptable for Latvian market placement; (3) DoC retention — the signed EU Declaration of Conformity must be retained for 10 years and be available to SPRK on request; (4) WEEE registration — WEEE compliance scheme registration with ZAAO or RecycleLV (Latvian producer compliance organisations) is required before market placement of EEE; (5) Online platform sales — sales via e-commerce platforms into Latvia are subject to the same EU AR and CE marking obligations; platforms are increasingly responsible for verifying compliance under GPSR and the Digital Services Act. Manufacturers should engage an EU AR service provider and ensure Latvian translations of labelling and instructions before first shipment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — EU AR or EU importer required before first placement in Latvia; Latvian-language labelling mandatory under Latvian consumer protection law; DoC retention 10 years (RED Art. 10); WEEE registration with ZAAO or RecycleLV required
mandatory_status.cn: No equivalent — CCC lists Chinese manufacturer address; no third-country AR structure required for Chinese domestic market

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] An EU Authorised Representative is a hard legal prerequisite for Chinese manufacturers without an EU importer selling wireless devices in Latvia. Latvian-language labelling is a national mandatory requirement beyond the EU-wide CE marking obligation. WEEE registration with ZAAO or RecycleLV is required before first Latvian market placement. Online platform sales into Latvia are subject to identical obligations. Failure to appoint an EU AR before first market placement is grounds for SPRK product withdrawal and RAPEX notification.

source.publisher: EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the European Union

rows.requirement: CE Marking — RED 2014/53/EU + SPRK Market Surveillance
rows.target_requirement: Latvia is an EU member state; the Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU applies directly and in full. All wireless and radio equipment placed on the Latvian market must bear the CE marking, backed by a signed EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC). The DoC must reference all applicable directives and harmonised standards (RED Art. 3.1(a) safety, Art. 3.1(b) EMC, Art. 3.2 radio performance, and Art. 3.3(d)-(f) cybersecurity where in scope). SPRK (Public Utilities Commission — Sabiedrisko pakalpojumu regulēšanas komisija) is Latvia's national market surveillance authority for RED; it conducts market checks, can issue withdrawal orders, and reports non-compliant products to the EU RAPEX/Safety Gate system. The Consumer Rights Protection Centre (PTAC — Patērētāju tiesību aizsardzības centrs) oversees general product safety market surveillance. CE marking must be affixed to the product or its packaging before placement; minimum marking height is 5 mm. Latvian-language labelling is required as Latvia's official language under EU labelling law.
target_standards: Directive 2014/53/EU (RED) — transposed into Latvian law via the Radio Equipment Law (Radioiekārtu likums) and related SPRK implementing regulations
Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 — market surveillance and conformity of products (SPRK as national authority for RED; PTAC for general product safety)
Decision 768/2008/EC — CE marking conformity assessment modules
Latvian Radio Equipment Law (Radioiekārtu likums) — national transposition of RED 2014/53/EU
rows.china_equivalent: In China, market access for wireless devices requires SRRC Type Approval (NRA/MIIT) for the radio transmitter module and, for IT equipment such as Wi-Fi routers and IoT gateways, CCC (China Compulsory Certification) under CNCA-C17-01. A separate MIIT Network Access Licence (NAL) is required for certain telecom terminal equipment. The SAMR supervises market surveillance through its provincial bureaus. Neither SRRC nor CCC confers CE marking or satisfies RED conformity assessment obligations in Latvia or any EU country.
china_standards: SRRC Type Approval — NRA/MIIT mandatory radio licence for wireless transmitters
CCC — China Compulsory Certification (CNCA-C17-01 for IT equipment)
MIIT Network Access Licence (NAL) — for telecom terminal equipment
rows.gap: CE marking under RED is a hard legal prerequisite for placing wireless devices on the Latvian market. SRRC and CCC are not recognised and cannot substitute. Key Latvia-specific points beyond the standard EU RED gap: (1) SPRK actively enforces RED through market surveillance and product withdrawals; PTAC supports general product safety enforcement; (2) Latvian-language labelling is mandatory — product name, manufacturer/EU AR name and address, model identifier, and intended use where not self-evident must appear in Latvian (Latin script); (3) Plug type C/F (Schuko) and 230 V/50 Hz must be confirmed for mains-powered devices; (4) WEEE registration with a Latvian producer compliance scheme (ZAAO or RecycleLV) is required before market placement of EEE; (5) Latvia's Riga Port is a growing Baltic Sea electronics distribution hub — products entering the Baltic corridor through Latvia are subject to Latvian CE compliance obligations at point of Latvian placement, even if onward shipment is intended. Chinese manufacturers must complete the full EU RED conformity assessment (testing, DoC, CE mark, EU AR appointment) before any shipment to Latvia.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — RED 2014/53/EU as transposed into Latvian law (Radioiekārtu likums); CE marking required before placement on Latvian market; SPRK enforces
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — SRRC Type Approval + CCC (where applicable) for Chinese domestic market; not recognised in Latvia

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking under RED 2014/53/EU is the primary market-access gate for wireless devices entering Latvia. SPRK enforces RED nationally; PTAC supports general product safety surveillance; non-compliant products are subject to withdrawal and RAPEX notification. SRRC and CCC are not recognised. Latvian-language labelling and WEEE registration with ZAAO/RecycleLV are additional mandatory obligations beyond the EU-wide CE marking requirement.
